newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: KPN reviews London, Frankfurt listings.
newsitem.headline: KPN reviews London, Frankfurt listings.

text.p: Dutch telecommunications and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Wednesday it was reviewing the cost effectiveness of its listings on the London and Frankfurt exchanges.
KPN chairman and chief executive Wim Dik said the company would complete a review next year of whether it should continue to be listed on the German and British stock exchanges.
"We are reviewing whether Frankfurt and London are worthwhile," Dik told a news conference in Sydney.
The news conference was held to announce KPN's A$2.0 billion agreed takeover bid for Australian-based transport group TNT Ltd.
Dik said if the review showed the dual listings were cost effective and worthwhile then it was possible KPN could eventually look at listing on the Australian Stock Exchange.
"But I'm not so sure this review will turn out to show these listings are worthwhile," he said.
KPN would welcome any TNT shareholders who wanted to maintain an exposure to TNT's assets after the acquisition.
Earlier on Wednesday, KPN launched a A$2.45 per share cash takeover bid for TNT that that was 50 percent above TNT's previous closing price and market capitalisation.
TNT's board recommended shareholders accept the bid and brokers said it was likely to be successful.
